entry.dc:title: PEABODY FOCUSES ON SURFACE MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: The application of industrial engineering techniques, combined with the development of computer-based systems analysis, is becoming a key management tool by which Peabody hopes to maximize its production output, improve control of its operations, and reduce its operating costs.

entry.dc:title: REGULATIONS COMPLICATE LAND RECLAMATION IN THE WEST.
entry.dc:creator: Seltz-Petrash A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Civil Engineering New York N Y
entry.dc:description: The 1977 Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act provides necessary protection to land during and after strip mining. However, according to the coal industry, some of the regulations are misguided - costing time and money but yielding no real environmental benefit. Article is an overview of some of the problems industry thinks are most severe. Sidebar on the basics of land reclamation after surface mining in the West.

entry.dc:title: COAL MINING TECHNOLOGY IN THE WESTERN UNITED STATES.
entry.dc:creator: Ramani R.V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: This paper gives a brief overview of the current status of underground and surface coal mining in the Western United States. Mining methods practised at six mines are reviewed to illustrate the technology of surface and underground methods. The advancing longwall at the Dutch Creek mine is the only one currently being practised in the country. Room and pillar operations will continue to be the most important underground mining method in the near future. Surface mining methods reviewed here are fairly standard for thick and multiple seams that are near surface. The greatest impact on surface mining industry is due to the current legislative, administrative, and public attitudes which make it necessary for a greater government-industry interaction on various planning, operation and reclamation aspects.

entry.dc:title: CHALLENGE OF FINANCING CANADIAN OIL SANDS DEVELOPMENT.
entry.dc:creator: McMillian J.
entry.dc:description: The author discusses the economic viability and methods available for financing major oil sands projects in Canada. The focus of the paper is directed at analyzing the estimated capital costs, operating costs and potential financing methods for the proposed Alsands surface mining project and the Cold Lake in situ project. The effect of royalties, taxes, capital availability and future oil prices are assessed in relation to these projects.

entry.dc:title: CAPTAIN MINE: A NATIONAL SHOWCASE FOR SURFACE MINING & RECLAMATION.
entry.dc:creator: Blakely W.
entry.dc:description: By using bucketwheel excavators, shovels, spreaders and a round-the-pit conveyor system, Southwestern Illinois Coal's Captain Mine has become a major producer while reclaiming its land.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING PROBLEMS RUN DEEP.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Steeply pitching multiple seams are hard to mine. Western producers use computerized engineering and a variety of equipment combinations to deal with them.

entry.dc:title: STATUS REPORT ON CANADIAN COAL MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Jamieson E.
entry.dc:description: How well is the Canadian coal industry able to expand in the tough competition with other fuels in Canada and with other suppliers in the international, metallurgical and thermal coal trade? Coal production as a whole decreased between 1950 and 1960 and, although there has been a tripling of production since then, underground production continued to decrease until 1975. This trend has been reversed to a certain extent as a result of the modernization of mines in Cape Breton, but in 1978 over 85% of coal production came from surface mining. Against this background, the paper reviews current Canadian mining operations. Conclusions are then drawn regarding some of the longer-term mining applications in relation to the latest coal demand forecast.

entry.dc:title: FRONT-END LOADERS: VERSATILE AND PRODUCTIVE MACHINES.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: Front-end wheel loaders are becoming an increasingly important tool to surface mining throughout the coal regions of the United States. Their extraordinary versatility is evidenced by the wide range of jobs that they are assigned to. The larger loaders efficiently strip overburden and dig and load coal. Smaller units maintain haul roads, build ditches and dikes, and excavate settling ponds. A survey is presented of different types and sizes of front-end loaders used in U. S. coal mines.

entry.dc:title: FORDING RIVER MINE - AN OVERVIEW.
entry.dc:creator: Urso P.
entry.dc:description: This paper discusses the mining problems encountered at the Fording River coal mine, B. C. , Canada, to date, and how they have been solved. All of the production now comes from surface mining, but underground hydraulic mining is planned and briefly described. Other facets of the operation, including markets, equipment and personnel, are covered.

entry.dc:title: COSMAR OVERVIEW.
entry.dc:creator: Cook C.
entry.dc:description: The Committee on Surface Mining and Reclamation (COSMAR) submitted its report to the Council on Environmental Quality and the Congress in 1979. The report, ″The Surface Mining of Noncoal Minerals,″ is briefly summarized.

entry.dc:title: MARTIN COUNTY'S MINING PRACTICES.
entry.dc:creator: Mason R.
entry.dc:description: Martin County Coal's mining practices are described, showing how the company achieves production goals by applying surface and underground extraction methods that are especially adapted to eastern Kentucky conditions. The 2 1/2-million-tpy producer mines four seams with two underground mines, four surface mines and three mine contractors. Mining by both methods helps assure that reserves will be recovered to the maximum. Surface mining accounts for 55% of total output, and underground contributes 45%.

entry.dc:title: 1980: ANOTHER YEAR OF (STUNTED) GROWTH.
entry.dc:creator: Guccione E.
entry.dc:description: A brief forecast is given for the U. S. coal industry's performance in 1980. Long-term US coal production is most likely to reach the 1-billion-tpy level in 1985. However, the short-term picture throughout 1980 is not expected to be appreciably better than it was in 1979. Although this year's U. S. coal production and consumption figures should surpass 1979's levels, excess capacity will continue in the eastern and western U. S. coal fields. Further, the coal industry is likely to get some relief from amendments to the Surface Mining and the Clean Air Acts. Salient figures for U. S. bituminous coal and lignite are given in accompanying tables.

entry.dc:title: Soil nitrogen relationships in spoil material generated by the surface mining of lignite coal
entry.dc:creator: Hons F.M.
entry.dc:description: Three acid, surface-mined soils and an adjacent undisturbed soil were evaluated for nitrification potentials and nonexchangeable NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N retention to better understand N mechanisms and improve the reclamation efficiency of these soils. The mined soils nitrified a maximum of only 7% of an added 100 ppm NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N, although the undisturbed soil nitrified 93% of the applied N. Total N digestion showed one mined soil to have a nonexchangeable NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N retention capacity of 6.2 meq/100g. Organically retained NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N accounted for 73% of the total retention. Another procedure utilizing differences in exchangeable NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N between moist and dried samples as estimates of nonexchangeable NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N retention, showed retentive capacities of the mined soils ranging from 4.1 to 7.8 meq NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N/100g. Lignite exhibited a retentive capacity of 46.0 meq NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N/100g. Nonexchangeable retention was significantly correlated with the residual lignite content of the soil. Low nitrification potentials and large nonexchangeable NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N retention capacities suggested that applied NH<inf>4</inf><sup>+</sup>-N fertilizers might be inefficient in the mined soils. © 1980 The Williams & Wilkins Co.

entry.dc:title: UI'S TRAPPER MINES THE HIGH COUNTRY.
entry.dc:creator: Jackson D.
entry.dc:description: A brief account is given of how Utah International (UI) is successfully solving some surface mining problems at its Trapper coal mine near Craig, Colo. Some of these involve surface mining at minus 45 degree F at an altitude of 6,800 ft, deep snow and difficult mountainous terrain, four coal seams that pitch at 16%, as well as scheduling mining activities at three different pits. The company uses three 30-cu-yd draglines in up-dip/down-dip cycles to remove overburden and interburden in the three pits, each containing two seams.

entry.dc:title: SUB-BITUMINOUS COAL RESOURCES IN THE WESTERN USA - THEIR EXPLOITATION AND UTILIZATION.
entry.dc:creator: Dunham R.K.
entry.dc:description: Recent increases in the price of oil have given significant impetus in the western U. S. to the exploitation and conversion of low rank sub-bituminous coals into either gaseous or liquid fuels. At the present time, emphasis is on surface mining but, in the longer term, the majority of this coal can be recovered only by underground methods. This article presents a review of the surface mining techniques in use and reviews the coal conversion techniques being investigated, including surface and underground gasification and a variety of liquefaction processes.

entry.dc:title: KEMMERER SURFACE-MINES 12 SEAMS.
entry.dc:creator: Jackson D.
entry.dc:description: This article highlights the successful coal mining operations of Kemmerer Coal Co. , a not-so-large but fast-growing western U. S. coal operator based in Wyoming. Using three surface mining methods - truck-shovel, dragline and scraper-dozer, the company mines a dozen seams with an aggregate thickness of 300 ft. Although the various pits works at different overburden-to-coal ratios, the overall mining operation is designed for an average 4:1 ratio. Kemmerer Coal's coal preparation and coal handling facilities are also described.

entry.dc:title: OPENCAST COAL IN BURGUNDY.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Extraction of coal by surface mining in France, while not extensive, is nevertheless of growing interest. Environmental considerations are of prime importance, particularly when operations are conducted close to towns and other industry. Rehabilitation may be required to improve the site for the benefit of the local community. This article surveys equipment and techniques used in opencast mining of coal at Montceau-les-Mines, Burgundy, France.

entry.dc:title: Research on the hydrology and water quality of watersheds subjected to surface mining. Phase 1: premining hydrologic and water quality conditions. Summary report 22 Jan 1976 - 22 Jan 1978.
entry.dc:creator: McIntosh G.
entry.dc:description: Five watersheds, ranging in size from 29 to 52 acres, were selected in east-central Ohio for the purpose of investigating the hydrologic and water quality conditions occurring before, during, and after surface mining. The average concentrations of the water quality parameters for all watersheds were as low or lower than the Environmental Protection Agency recommended maximum allowable concentrations in drinking water except for suspended solids.-from STAR, 18(18), 1980

entry.dc:title: Characterization of vegetation and drainage in strip mined land utilizing remote sensing techniques. Final report.
entry.dc:creator: Johannsen C.J.
entry.dc:description: Research conducted during this project has utilized remote sensing images and data to study surface vegetation identification, vegetation biomass and drainage patterns of coal strip mined land. Study sites were located in Boone, Randolph and Macon counties in central Missouri. This report presents the results of surface vegetation and drainage analyses of those sites and methodologies used for accurate, timely and useful applications of remotely gathered data for monitoring coal surface mining reclamation activities. -from US Govt Reports Announcements, 2, 1980

entry.dc:title: Environmental assessment of surface mining methods: head-of- hollow fill and mountaintop removal. Interim report Nov 75 - January 77
entry.dc:creator: Robins J.
entry.dc:description: The study explores the environmental impact of the mining and reclamation techniques employed in West Virginia and Kentucky mountaintop removal and head-of-hollow fill sites. The project is divided into four major phases, the first three of which are discussed in this Interim Report: I. State-of-the-Art Review, II. General Environmental Assessment of West Virginia and Kentucky Mines Sites, III. Intensive Mine Site Monitoring and Environmental Assessment in Both States, and IV. Evaluation and Update of Construction Guidelines. -from US Govt Reports Announcement, 26, 1979

entry.dc:title: Coal surface mining reclamation.
entry.dc:creator: Rowe J.E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Vance Bibliographies Public Administration Series Bibliography
entry.dc:description: The degree of environmental degradation caused by coal surface mining can be controlled by the enforcement of strict standards. This bibliography examines the many environmental, legal and economic factors affecting reclamation, but it omits the large number of studies concerning soil conditions, tree/vegetation species, wildlife habitat, and other biological/ecological factors associated with surface mining reclamation. About 350 references, mainly to periodical and report literature, arranged alphabetically by author, are given.-after Author

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING TECHNOLOGY, PRACTICES, AND PLANS AND GULF COAST LIGNITE.
entry.dc:creator: Russell J.E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Industrial and Engineering Chemistry Product Research and Development
entry.dc:description: Lignite resources of 20 billion tons are estimated for the Gulf Coast Region. Geology of deposits and analyses of the lignites are given. Exploration techniques and leasing practices are reviewed. Necessary mining permits and regulatory agencies are listed for the five Gulf Coast states. In addition, several Federal, state, county and local agencies require permits of notification. These agencies are summarized for Texas. Feasibility studies, mine development, and mining operations are discussed. In 1979, the only operating surface mines were in Texas, with 84 pct of total production used in electrical power generation by one utility. Over 20 million tons were mined in 1978, and projections indicate production of 65 million tons in 1985. Reclamation of mined land is satisfactory. Impact of extensive development on water, air, and socieconomic factors are reviewed.

entry.dc:title: IMPLICATIONS OF RCRA, SMCRA, AND TSCA ON UNDERGROUND COAL GASIFICATION.
entry.dc:creator: Hagen A.A.
entry.prism:publicationName: American Society of Mechanical Engineers Applied Mechanics Division AMD
entry.dc:description: This paper presents an assessment of the implications of current legislative and regulatory actions associated with the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act (SMCRA), and Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) on underground coal gasification. RCRA and TSCA regulations are not final; however, under the regulations as currently proposed, liquids and tars condensed from UCG product gas stream will be classified hazardous wastes, requiring application of prescribed waste disposal techniques. Options will include use of incinerators meeting specific design and performance criteria, or storage and disposal that must be documented through s manifest system for up to 20 years. TSCA premanufacture notice of chemical substances may apply. SMCRA regulations are final, and coal in situ processing is to be regulated under underground mining provisions.

entry.dc:title: USDA teamwork in reclamation.
entry.dc:creator: Unger D.
entry.dc:description: Introductory remarks to a symposium on surface mining and reclamation. The new voluntary programme is called RAMP (Rural Abandoned Mine Program). The role of USDA is outlined. -Jennifer Clayton

entry.dc:title: The protection of hydrologic and land preservation values under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977: a welcome reform ( West Virginia).
entry.dc:creator: Woley D.
entry.dc:description: The 1977 Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act (Act) is evaluated in the context of West Virginia's 1971 Surface Mining and Reclamation Act. Several land use considerations are discussed in relation to the federal Act. The public participation aspects of the Act are outlined in a typical scenario.-from Selected Water Resources Abstracts Strip mining strip mine wastes surface runoff soil conservation water pollution control land fills public rights sediment control land use government finance governmental interrelations hydrology.
